18: Great is peace. For the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, that is written in holiness, may be erased to make peace between a man and his wife. Rabbi Meir was sitting and expounding on Friday night. There was a woman there who heard his voice and found it pleasant. She waited until he was finished and went home and found that the light was extinguished [it had gotten late]. Her husband said to her, "Where have you been?" She said to him, "I was sitting and listening to the voice of a preacher." He swore that she could not come in until she spat in  [R. Meir's] face. He expelled her from his house, and she was three months away. [That was] until R. Meir came towards her and found her with [other] women. He said, "Perhaps there is one among you who knows how to say a charm into the eye, as my eyes are teary." Her neighbors said to her, "Behold the Omnipresent has already done your will to make him stumble." So she spit in his face and left. He said to her, "Say [to your husband], 'You told me once, but I already spit seven times.'" His students said to him, "You disgraced the Torah so much?" He said to them, "It is enough for a slave to be like his master. Is it not enough for Meir to be the same as his Maker? As behold, the great name that is written in purity is erased in the water in order to make peace between a man and his wife!
